A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TuRBO-ENN research work. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization experiments on 51 analytic functions, five reinforcement-learning environments and MOPTA08, plus component ablations and K sensitivity results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original natural- and frozen-noise optimization experiments on five tasks, with performance curves and timing results. Figure 1 also reports an analytic-function timing study.

M1.justification: V1 uses an unfitted distance-weighted ENN surrogate with Pareto-front acquisition. V2 adds aleatoric variance, hyperparameter fitting through subsampled leave-one-out pseudolikelihood, noise-aware incumbent selection and UCB with beta=1. The original fitting-free approach remains as the noise-free variant.

E1.justification: V2 adds BipedalWalker-v3, Push-v5, LASSO-DNA and natural-noise scenarios, while removing Swimmer-v5, Ant-v5, Humanoid-v5 and MOPTA08. LunarLander and Hopper remain. Analytic evaluation narrows from a 51-function optimization-quality suite to a 12-function timing study.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds sparse-GP UCB and Vecchia comparators and removes Log-EI, while retaining ordinary UCB, Optuna and TuRBO. Simulator comparisons retain random search, CMA-ES and the renamed TuRBO variants; v2 explicitly excludes Optuna from frozen-noise Hopper after exceeding its compute budget.

E3.justification: V2 introduces natural-noise evaluation using held-out seeds and passive expected-return estimates, alongside revised frozen-noise budgets. For example, the 50-arm Hopper setting changes from 50 to 10 denoising seeds and extends to 50,000 observations. V2's natural-noise LunarLander budget is internally inconsistent: Table 1 lists 300 observations, whereas Figure 3 plots 10,000.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix A's mean-only, uncertainty-only, randomized-uncertainty ablations and K sweep disappear, including Figures 10–11. V2 retains the surrogate-free ablation as turbo-zero and examines its behavior under natural versus frozen noise, but provides no replacement component or K sensitivity study.

E5.justification: The reported simulator replication count changes from 100 in v1 to 30 in v2. V1 introduces mean plus/minus one-standard-error plots; v2 explicitly specifies mean plus/minus two standard errors for its simulator results. These are revisions to replication and error-band reporting, without new significance tests.

E6.justification: V1's analytic rank-score and appendix ablation results disappear, while v2 reports new natural/frozen-noise curves and timings. For the retained 50-arm/50-seed LunarLander configuration, TuRBO/ENN total times change from 67.5/0.3 seconds in v1 Figure 6c to 52.2/0.6 seconds in v2 Table 1. Replication counts also change, so these updates do not isolate a method-level speed change.

T1.justification: V2 adds noisy-surrogate and subsampled-likelihood derivations. Its new Appendix A introduces compactness, continuity and noiselessness assumptions, local-consistency and uncertainty lemmas, an acquisition improvement argument and a convergence theorem. V1 has no corresponding convergence analysis. The new theorem concerns a noiseless scalarized acquisition variant.

C1.justification: The claim of substantially faster proposals with competitive solution quality remains. V2 additionally claims linear-time fitting and acquisition for noisy objectives, scaling to 50,000 observations and a PseudoBO convergence guarantee. V1's broadly fitting-free narrative becomes a noise-free special case.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of natural-noise difficulty and the reduced effectiveness of surrogate-free search. Section 6 adds limitations involving joint sampling, high-dimensional distances, constrained/mixed/multiobjective problems and absent regret bounds. V1's explicit analytic-performance shortfall against LEI/UCB and associated global-search discussion are removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1, explicit fitting and incumbent-selection instructions, controller specifications, and shared/held-out seed handling. V1's explicit candidate count, function-distortion recipe and estimated 30,000 CPU-hours disappear. Code locations remain anonymized, and v2 leaves the likelihood subsample size P unspecified numerically.

R1.justification: Section 3 substantially expands positioning against sparse GPs and Vecchia/nearest-neighbor GPs, with corresponding new citations. V2 also connects ENN to Chen and Lam's PseudoBO framework and introduces a stronger claim about principled uncertainty quantification relative to other non-GP surrogates.

P1.justification: The abstract, method exposition, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 adds an explicit contribution list, reorganizes experiments around task descriptions and noise handling, and replaces the ablation appendix with a structured theoretical appendix. These exceed terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: V2 switches to two-column layout, redraws the timing and surrogate figures, and replaces simulator displays with natural/frozen-noise pairs. The Pareto illustration, analytic-quality plots and appendix ablation figures disappear. A new algorithm box and task-specific timing table substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful held-out natural-noise evaluations, relevant scalable-GP timing baselines and clearer algorithm documentation. However, it removes component/K ablations and broad analytic-quality evidence. Its new convergence claim exceeds the demonstrated scope: Appendix A analyzes a noiseless scalarized rule, without establishing the guarantee for the implemented acquisition rules. The LunarLander figure/table budget mismatch further weakens result traceability. These material gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
